title: F2 proponent: two-systems / masked-English / stego as 3-layer composition (LESSON-022 shape)
hypothesis_summary: Sanborn has publicly stated K4 uses 'two systems' and contains 'masked English'. The project's epistemic policy treats Sanborn's statements as Tier-3 community hearsay, NOT public fact (see feedback_sanborn_epistemic_weight). The proponent reading interprets this as a 3-layer hand-cipher composition: a substitution layer, a keyed columnar transposition, and a rail-fence transposition (LESSON-022 shape). Tested with the disclosed-crib core keyword pool (BERLIN, CLOCK, EAST, NORTHEAST, KRYPTOS) so that the 'masked English' reading retains Tier-1 keyword evidence even when the composition framing is Tier-3.

provenance_items.quote_or_summary: Sanborn publicly stated K4 uses two encryption systems. Tier-3 hearsay per project policy.

composition_templates.rationale: LESSON-022 three-role: substitution + keyed columnar + rail-fence depth. The 'two systems' phrase admits a sub+trans+trans reading.
Beaufort variant of the same three-role composition.

constraints: Three-role independent assignment per LESSON-022 generator. Allowed depths restricted to small rail counts.
caveats: PROPONENT framing for the Tier-3 'two-systems' claim. The claim ITSELF is creator-statement hearsay; this pack tests one structural realization of it.
Sanborn's two-systems claim does not specify what 'system' means — it could mean two cipher layers, two alphabets, or stego+cipher. This pack picks one structural interpretation.
